description:
`cargo test --release -p kopi-beans --lib` fails a stable-ish SET of tests but an UNSTABLE COUNT -- observed 8, 9, and 10 failures across consecutive runs of the same binary, no code change in between. Pre-existing on main at 0aaf4ee (confirmed by stashing an unrelated change and re-running), so NOT a regression from the gix 0.87.1 bump filed as bd-ci9.

The recurring names:

    daemon::runtime::core::tests::restores_hlc_state_for_non_daemon_actor
    daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_allocates_dot_counter_in_wal_index_without_rewriting_store_meta
    daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_atomic_commit_failpoint_rolls_back_event_and_watermark
    daemon::runtime::executor::tests::mutation_span_includes_realtime_context
    daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::bootstrap_crash_before_meta_commit_recovers_on_next_open
    daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::phase3_head_sha_loads_from_index
    daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::runtime_upgrades_stale_index_meta_and_rebuilds_legacy_index
    daemon::runtime::store::runtime::tests::stale_pending_marker_does_not_rollback_later_committed_meta
    git::sync::tests::migrate_store_ref_to_v2_dry_run_peeks_remote_without_mutating_tracking_ref

All of them touch shared daemon/store state, so the likely cause is cross-test interference under cargo's parallel test threads (shared store dir / global HLC / a daemon singleton) rather than nine independent bugs. Worth checking whether `--test-threads=1` goes green -- if it does, that localises it to isolation, not logic.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a permanently-red suite means the release gate can't tell a real regression from the usual noise. Verifying the gix bump needed a stash-and-compare against baseline precisely because `test result: FAILED` on its own said nothing.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: SCOPE CORRECTION: git::sync::tests::migrate_store_ref_to_v2_dry_run_peeks_remote_without_mutating_tracking_ref is ALREADY tracked as bd-aws / gh-60 -- and it is a DETERMINISTIC failure (OrSetV1 vs LegacyEdges assertion at crates/kopi-beans/src/git/sync.rs:3279), not part of the flakiness described here. Exclude it. This bead covers the EIGHT daemon::runtime::* tests only, whose distinguishing symptom is the wobbling count (8/9/10 across identical consecutive runs) that points at cross-test interference rather than a logic bug.

title: kopi-beans daemon/store tests flaky: 8-10 failures, count wobbles run to run

description:
GH: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/12
Part of the CJK / annotated-PDF field report (2026-08-01), epic bd-ski.
Original write-up: docs/issues/field-report-2026-08-01/

--- original GH body, verbatim ---


> Part of the **pdf2md CJK/annotated-PDF** work order — see the tracking issue for shared context, the corrections in §0, and the additive-corruption principle these cards rest on.

**Confidence:** High (reproduced 2026-08-01). **Owns:** `apps/cli/src/main.rs`

## Problem

Orienting in this repo, `kopitiam tokens crates/ --tree` reported:

```
crates/  74135961 tokens (22673 files)
  kopitiam-ai/  66959903 tokens (20830 files)
    vendor/  66903180 tokens (20813 files)
      OpenFOAM-dev/  40633875 tokens (17566 files)
        tutorials/ ...
```

**90% of the reported total is `kopitiam-ai/vendor/OpenFOAM-dev`**, mostly CFD mesh geometry. The first 25 lines of output were entirely vendored tutorials.

The tool built to make budgeting cheap gave an answer dominated by files no agent will ever read, and I had to re-run with explicit crate paths.

## Change

Default-exclude `vendor/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.git/`; add `--include-vendor` to restore.

**Preferred:** report them as a single collapsed line rather than omitting silently —

```
vendor/  66959903 tokens (20813 files) [excluded]
```

— which is honest and equally cheap.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `tokens crates/ --tree` surfaces the real source tree within the first screen.
- [ ] Vendored totals shown as one collapsed line, not expanded.
- [ ] `--include-vendor` restores current behaviour.
